newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner in German pulp deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner in German pulp deal.

text.p: Norway's Kvaerner ASA said on Wednesday it had entered an agreement with Thyssen Rheinstahl Technik GmbH, Kloeckner Industrie-Anlagen GmbH and Altmark-Industrie AG to form a company to build the world's largest pulp plant.
The plant, to be called Zellstoff Stendal GmbH, will have a capacity of 500,000 tonnes per year of long-fibre pulp and will cost five to six billion crowns.
Kvaerner's share of the investment will be 2.1 billion crowns ($325.2 million), the company said in a statement to the Oslo bourse.
